answer: Recursive Memory Degradation Tax. Every identity node or vertex in the network must maintain a unique, cryptographically signed audit trail of state transitions anchored to a global cryptographic beacon. The enforcement rule requires each identity to pay an escalating compute fee proportional to the network-wide density of correlated state updates. When a sybil attacker spins up thousands of concurrent identities, they trigger a sudden storm of synchronization overhead that acts like a gale, exponentially multiplying the state-processing cost per identity.
